ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); record that the driver's cancellation did not meet the required wait time under NS-1(iii).
ruling.reasoning: The driver cancelled this RydeX trip, so the cancellation-fee branch runs through NS-0's driver-cancellation path and, the driver claiming a rider no-show, through NS-1/NS-2 [F4][NS-0]. The arrival-confirmation elements are settled in the driver's favour: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:07:15 and the GPS put him 40 m from the pickup at that moment, the closest approach overall being 32 m [F6][F1][NS-1]. The decisive element fails: after the tap he remained inside the 200 m radius for only 470 s continuously (7 min 50 s), short of the 480 s (8 min, at least) threshold the case record sets for a no-show, so NS-1(iii) is not met and the trace marks it ✗ [F6][F2][NS-1]. His own chat message "8 min up, cancelling the trip" at 09:14 likewise precedes the cancellation by only about a minute after the tap, consistent with the shortfall [F10][F6]. Under NS-2, where any of NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) is not fulfilled the $6.61 (here the recorded $5.00) cancellation fee must be refunded in full, so the fee charged on the record must be returned [F7][F4][NS-2]. The companion flag branch of NS-2 does not apply: the tap was made while genuinely at the pickup (40 m), so this is not a fake confirmation, and no account action is warranted [F6][F1][NS-2]. The rider's account shows no upheld no-show dispute and no prior flag basis under RD-6 or NS-2 arises here [F16][F17][RD-6][NS-2]. The rider's own account of coming out "a minute after" cancellation does not affect the outcome, which turns wholly on the driver's side of NS-1(iii) [F4][NS-1].
